evidence.title: Court of Appeals CA-G.R. SP Nos. 70014 / 104604 public reproduction
evidence.notes: Public reproduction describes the Republic's jurisdiction, notice, reconstitution and extrinsic-fraud challenges and records material disputes over 3957-P. Certified CA rollo/disposition remains the preferred P1 source.

contradictions.description: Later appellate material questions why the purported 4 Feb 1972 Decision with Compromise Agreement bears the same date as the purported filing of the amended petition. Original docket timestamps and hearing minutes are required.

The original 1972 record and the later post-fire reconstitution proceedings must be separated. Invalidity of a reconstitution process does not automatically prove nonexistence of an original judgment, and existence of an original judgment does not establish the validity of later reconstructed copies.

The Republic challenged subject-matter jurisdiction to reconstitute Torrens titles in what it characterized as an ordinary civil action for quieting/recovery. This directly affects legal effect even if a document is physically authentic.

The Republic alleged failure to satisfy mandatory publication and notice requirements to occupants, adjoining owners and interested parties. Due-process compliance must be established from the primary record.
Official Supreme Court litigation confirms downstream 3957-P enforcement was enjoined by the Court of Appeals. Present enforceability cannot be assumed without the complete appellate history.
